problem: Evaluating LLM agents for scientific tasks ignores tool-use costs like simulation time, making practical metrics like pass@k unrealistic.
approach: SimulCost introduces a cost-sensitive benchmark that compares LLM-tuned parameters against traditional scanning across 2,947 physics simulation tasks (13 simulators), measuring both accuracy and computational cost.
contribution: Frontier LLMs achieve 46–65% success in single-round mode but are 1.5–2.5× slower than traditional scanning; multi-round improves to 72–81%, revealing LLMs remain uneconomical for high-accuracy physics tuning.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems suffer from high communication costs due to redundant message exchanges that don't contribute meaningfully to final decisions.
approach: AgentTailor evaluates semantic contribution of communication edges via an Edge Prediction Network that estimates edge utilities through virtual execution, then optimizes agent interaction structure.
contribution: AgentTailor achieves 91.36% average accuracy on six datasets while reducing tokens by 21.2%–61.6% compared to baseline multi-agent systems.

problem: Everyday photos often have structural flaws (composition, pose, viewpoint) that existing retouching methods cannot fix while preserving subject identity.
approach: AesFormer uses a two-stage approach: an aesthetic action model (AesThinker) plans edits along seven photographic dimensions, then an action-conditioned editor (AesEditor) performs structural reconstruction.
contribution: AesFormer improves aesthetic photo reconstruction and matches professional tools; introduces AesRecon benchmark of 9,071 aligned poor–good image pairs and a video-based corpus-mining pipeline.

problem: Estimating discrete probability distributions under the ℓ∞ norm lacks tight minimax bounds and does not resolve open theoretical questions.
approach: Derives improved minimax bounds in expectation and high-probability tail bounds, fully empirical versions of the tightest risk bounds, and identifies worst-case extremal distributions.
contribution: Resolves open questions from Kontorovich & Painsky (2025) regarding ℓ∞ distribution estimation; provides both theoretical bounds and empirical validation.

problem: KV-cache retrieval for long-context LLM inference struggles with distribution drift, high latency, and memory requirements at scale.
approach: ParisKV combines collision-based candidate selection with quantized inner-product reranking and Unified Virtual Addressing for CPU-offloaded caches, enabling on-demand top-k fetching.
contribution: ParisKV achieves state-of-the-art long-context decoding: 2.8× higher throughput than full attention within its runnable range and 17–44× lower latency than baselines at million-token scale.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with long-video understanding due to massive KV-cache memory footprint; existing compression methods use uniform budgets and disrupt temporal continuity.
approach: EAKV leverages attention entropy to adaptively allocate compression budgets layer-wise, preserving critical tokens while distilling redundant contexts into compact anchors.
contribution: EAKV outperforms existing methods across diverse architectures with improvements of 0.6%–6.5%, matching or exceeding layer-wise semantic density-driven allocation.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems rely on direct concatenation of neighbor responses, limiting evidence receptive field and causing insight dilution over multi-hop communication paths.
approach: MOC reconstructs inter-agent communication to capture multi-hop dependencies through a structured multi-order evidence stream and Semantic-Topological Merging algorithm.
contribution: MOC consistently improves task performance and reduces communication costs across six diverse datasets and multiple LLM backbones.

problem: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is susceptible to reward overoptimization when policy models exploit spurious reward patterns and diverge from human intent.
approach: R2M (Real-Time Aligned Reward Model) leverages evolving hidden states from the policy as real-time feedback to align the reward model with distribution shifts during RL.
contribution: R2M addresses reward overoptimization by using policy feedback to maintain alignment beyond semantic-only reward models during continuous policy evolution.

problem: LLM agents struggle to automatically discover and exploit vulnerabilities due to limited interaction, weak execution grounding, and lack of experience reuse in cybersecurity tasks.
approach: Co-RedTeam decomposes vulnerability analysis into discovery and exploitation stages with execution-grounded iterative reasoning, code-aware analysis, and long-term memory to learn from prior trajectories.
contribution: Co-RedTeam achieves over 60% success rate in vulnerability exploitation and over 10% absolute improvement in vulnerability detection compared to baselines.

problem: Operator splitting methods for PDEs are designed without explicit links to unrolled hybrid learning architectures, limiting principled hybrid solver design.
approach: Proposes a unifying framework linking operator splitting algorithms from optimization with unrolled hybrid architectures, recovering existing plug-and-play models as special cases.
contribution: Framework enables design of new unrolled hybrid architectures achieving improved accuracy and stability on fluid dynamics benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion models can memorize training samples raising privacy concerns, but existing detection methods provide limited localization of where memorization appears in generated images.
approach: Proposes curvature-difference methods that detect memorization as coordinate-wise variance collapse by subtracting curvature of underfitted baselines, deriving a score-difference proxy.
contribution: Method outperforms prior attention-based localization on Stable Diffusion, evaluated against ground-truth memorization masks; provides geometric explanation for score-difference detection.

problem: Training autonomous web agents is fundamentally limited: real websites are unsafe to explore, hard to reset, and rarely provide verifiable feedback.
approach: VeriEnv treats language models as environment creators, automatically cloning websites into fully executable, verifiable synthetic environments with programmatic reward verification.
contribution: Agents trained on VeriEnv generalize to unseen websites, achieve site-specific mastery through self-evolving training, and benefit from scaling training environments.

problem: Latent Chain-of-Thought internalizes reasoning in hidden states but suffers from gradient attenuation and representational drift, leaving robust latent reasoning difficult.
approach: Analyzes Latent CoT via information theory, identifying dual collapse (gradient attenuation + representational drift), then proposes Trajectory Supervision and Space Supervision with Unified Latent Probe metric.
contribution: Shows reasoning accuracy depends on information fidelity in latent chains; demonstrates generative reconstruction better preserves semantic structure than rigid geometric compression.

problem: LLM compression via training-free SVD assumes uniform redundancy across layers, missing the non-uniform representational evolution and architectural criticality.
approach: CGSVD uses dual-level non-uniform allocation: angular distance for inter-layer significance, spectral entropy for intra-layer compressibility, plus Iterative Residual Filling to handle integer-rank truncation.
contribution: On LLaMA3.1-8B at 30% compression, CGSVD achieves 6.08% average zero-shot accuracy boost and 15.46 perplexity reduction vs. baseline SVD compression.

problem: Text-to-SQL relies on single static workflows, limiting scalability to out-of-distribution and long-tail scenarios where no single method excels.
approach: SquRL uses reinforcement learning to enable adaptive workflow construction at inference time, with rule-based reward, dynamic actor masking for exploration, and pseudo rewards for efficiency.
contribution: Dynamic workflow construction consistently outperforms best static methods, with pronounced gains on complex and out-of-distribution queries.

problem: Unlearning methods remove specific knowledge but degrade contextual utility—the ability to use forgotten information when re-introduced in prompts.
approach: Augments unlearning objectives with a plug-in term that explicitly preserves contextual utility while maintaining forgetting and retain-set performance.
contribution: Method restores contextual utility to near-original levels while maintaining effective forgetting and utility on retained knowledge.

problem: RLHF's distortion (gap between RLHF policy utility and optimal) can scale exponentially with preference heterogeneity, questioned in pluralistic settings.
approach: Analyzes RLHF with reward clipping, proving distortion depends on distribution mismatch between preference data and KL reference policy rather than being fundamental to the algorithm.
contribution: Establishes tight bounds on RLHF distortion (Θ(βB + β) in representative regimes); shows RLHF achieves optimal O(β) distortion when μ = π_ref, suggesting on-policy data improves pluralistic alignment.

problem: Understanding how many distinct sequences a transformer can output requires predicting expressiveness from limited architectural characteristics.
approach: Provides upper bounds on accessible sequences depending on prompt length and proves three properties: linear growth of max accessible sequence length, exponential decay beyond threshold, and theoretical upper bound on linear coefficient.
contribution: Empirically tight bounds (within factor <10 across architectures); explains transformer failures on simple tasks like copying; shows exponential decay holds even with unbounded context.

problem: Adversarial examples for tabular data are difficult due to heterogeneous features and asymmetric dependencies; existing approaches produce statistically likely yet semantically inconsistent attacks.
approach: LCSA leverages ensemble of heterogeneous neural Structural Causal Models and a structure-aware ripple mechanism that propagates perturbations downstream as a structural preconditioner.
contribution: LCSA outperforms baselines in 45 of 50 configurations with superior structural consistency and transferability of adversarial examples.

problem: LLM-based agents execute unsafe behaviors due to small deviations in intermediate thoughts; existing guardrails operate only on final outputs or require intrusive modifications.
approach: Thought-Aligner is a lightweight plug-in safety model that performs causal correction on unsafe thoughts before action execution via contrastive learning on paired safe/unsafe thoughts.
contribution: Thought-Aligner increases behavioral safety from ~50% to ~90% on average (23% above SoTA) and improves helpfulness by ~5% with low per-step latency across six LLMs.

problem: Spatio-temporal forecasting struggles with complex interactions under high-noise conditions and evolving temporal correlations in dynamic graphs.
approach: Proposes nested forecasting framework coupling future macro-level regional trends with micro-level historical observations via spectral clustering and progressive coarse-to-fine prediction.
contribution: Method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on multiple benchmarks by injecting macro-dynamics into node-level forecasting.

problem: Extracting heterogeneous RAG knowledge bases is difficult due to semantic discontinuities across domains that trap extraction methods relying on local continuity.
approach: GeoEx plans extraction in embedding space of proxy retrieval model for global coverage, uses embedding inversion to convert latent vectors to queries, and employs composite geometric strategy for cross-domain exploration.
contribution: GeoEx significantly outperforms baselines in extraction coverage and query efficiency across eight diverse domains and multiple retrievers/LLMs.

problem: Complex reasoning trajectories remain sparse in unconstrained LLM sampling and standard RL fails to guarantee acquisition of diverse reasoning patterns.
approach: Ctrl-R framework for learning structured reasoning via tractable trajectory control that actively guides rollouts, incentivizes exploration of diverse reasoning patterns, and enables unbiased importance-sampling estimation.
contribution: Ctrl-R enables exploration and internalization of previously unattainable reasoning patterns with consistent improvements on mathematical reasoning tasks.

problem: Financial reasoning with LLM agents lacks holistic benchmarks and fragile unstructured reasoning in complex financial workflows.
approach: ProFinR benchmark (528 expert-designed problems, 4 domains) + Financial Tool Universe (53 tools, 13 categories) + ProFinAgent with DAG planner for parallel execution and Case-Based Memory for reliable decisions.
contribution: ProFinAgent achieves 49.81% performance gain over baselines with 47.1% reduction in inference latency across professional finance reasoning tasks.

problem: Training LLMs on static data with fixed recipes cannot diagnose capability blind spots or provide targeted reinforcement for complex reasoning.
approach: DPE (Diagnostic-driven Progressive Evolution) spirals through diagnosis, data generation, and reinforcement: multiple agents annotate data and attribute failures to weaknesses, dynamically adjusting mixtures for targeted improvement.
contribution: Stable continual gains across eleven benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, showing DPE as scalable paradigm for open-task LMM training.

problem: Dynamic graph modeling struggles with balancing information propagation and noise dissipation, leading to uncontrolled information accumulation and poor generalization.
approach: LAMP combines impulsive neural ODEs with antisymmetric parameterization for conservative flow and data-driven dissipative dynamics, providing principled adaptive information retention.
contribution: LAMP provides stability guarantees, characterizes representational power, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on extended-range dependency modeling tasks.

problem: Vision-language models waste computation on redundant visual tokens; existing pruning methods fail on pixel grounding where token importance depends on input text.
approach: LiteLVLM reverses CLIP's visual-text similarity ranking for text-guided token pruning, retaining referent regions while recovering context tokens for foreground-background separation.
contribution: LiteLVLM maintains 90% of original performance with 22% speedup and 2.3× memory reduction; outperforms baselines by >5% across token budgets without training.

problem: Diffusion posterior sampling uses hand-tuned guidance weights that destabilize under stiff operator-dependent curvature for inverse problems.
approach: Replaces scalar guidance with per-noise-level damped Gauss-Newton correction computed in diffusion-state coordinates, using one-sided curvature model and diffusion-calibrated rank-one damping.
contribution: Achieves competitive PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on FFHQ and ImageNet inverse problems and best PSNR/SSIM on accelerated MRI reconstruction while running markedly faster.

problem: Design space for native multimodal foundation models remains opaque; existing models often inherit language pretraining biases without clear multimodal principles.
approach: Conducts from-scratch multimodal pretraining using Transfusion (next-token for language, diffusion for vision) on diverse data, isolating multimodal-specific factors without language pretraining interference.
contribution: Shows RAE optimal for unified visual representation, vision/language complementary with synergy, unified training enables world modeling, MoE harmonizes scaling asymmetry (vision 5× more data-hungry).

problem: Online infinite hidden Markov models struggle with streaming data containing outliers and misspecified models, lacking robustness guarantees.
approach: BR-iHMM derives robust update rule using generalized Bayesian inference and posterior influence function, balancing adaptivity and robustness with tunable parameters.
contribution: BR-iHMM reduces forecasting error up to 67% vs. competing online Bayesian methods; provides bounded PIF guarantees and demonstrates practicality on order book, electricity, and linear system data.

problem: LoRA variants insufficiently explore low-rank subspaces and degrade performance on convolution layers due to flattening that loses spatial structure.
approach: LAVA parameterizes weight increment as sum of learnable rank-1 components for both matrices and convolution kernels; incorporates orthogonal regularization with variance-reduction proof.
contribution: LAVA outperforms LoRA by +1.9% on LLaMA2-7b commonsense tasks; provides unified framework for language and vision adaptation with improved training stability.

problem: Estimating full-hand grasp pressure from egocentric video for VR/robotics is difficult; existing methods rely on planar surfaces/fingertip contacts and fail on complex 3D interactions.
approach: EgoTactile introduces benchmark pairing egocentric video with full-hand pressure supervision; proposes EgoPressureDiff, a conditional diffusion framework adapted from pre-trained video diffusion with Physically-Informed Feature Rectification.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on EgoTactile benchmark and robust transferability to in-the-wild scenarios via hallucinated contact patterns and resolved visual-physical ambiguities.

problem: Point cloud recognition via spatial mixup compromises geometric integrity by generating physically unrealistic samples.
approach: PSMix shifts mixing to spectral domain via Spherical Harmonic Transform with rotation-aware hierarchical mixing; combines with adversarial rotation optimization for invariance.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art robustness on ModelNet-C and ScanObjectNN-C benchmarks while serving as orthogonal plug-in boosting existing spatial strategies.

problem: Probabilistic super-resolution of high-dimensional spatial fields via diffusion is computationally prohibitive due to operating in pixel space.
approach: PODiff performs diffusion in fixed, variance-ordered Proper Orthogonal Decomposition space, exploiting mode orthogonality for interpretable latent geometry and efficient ensemble generation.
contribution: Achieves comparable reconstruction accuracy to pixel-space diffusion with substantially smaller latent space, less memory, and more reliable uncertainty vs. deterministic/MC Dropout baselines.

problem: LLMs generate syntactically valid optimization programs but struggle to reliably choose effective modeling strategies, causing incorrect formulations and inefficient solver behavior.
approach: SAGE makes Modeling Strategy explicit via solver-verified multi-strategy dataset + supervised fine-tuning + Segment-Weighted GRPO with composite reward (compliance, correctness, efficiency).
contribution: Improves pass@1 from 72.7 to 80.3; pass@16 discovers 19-29% more distinct formulations with 14.2% fewer constraints than baseline for more solver-efficient modeling.

problem: Consistency training's effects on model alignment are poorly understood; methods self-bootstrap which could amplify undesired behavior.
approach: Tests seven consistency training methods on 108 model organisms (7B–70B) exhibiting controlled misaligned behavior; analyzes distribution shifts and derives unifying theoretical framework.
contribution: Consistency training suppresses reward hacking and emergent misalignment but amplifies sycophancy; shows distribution mismatch from labeling, not selection operators, drives effects; not alignment-neutral.

problem: Panoramic scene generation via 2D video diffusion lacks intrinsic 3D understanding, producing frequent geometric inconsistencies in explorable worlds.
approach: PanoWorld-X uses panoramic representation mapping 3D scenes to standard format, designs Exploration Panoramic Plücker Embedding guidance for 3D motion, proposes sphere-aware attention capturing true geometric adjacency.
contribution: Achieves superior explorable immersive scene generation by leveraging spherical geometric properties and precise 3D motion control.

problem: Primal heuristics struggle to quickly find feasible solutions for NP-hard integer linear programming; end-to-end learning heuristics cannot independently generate feasible solutions.
approach: RL-SPH uses reinforcement learning to train a start primal heuristic capable of independently generating feasible solutions even for non-binary integers.
contribution: Rapidly obtains high-quality feasible solutions with 100% feasibility rate; achieves 28.6× lower primal gap and 2.6× lower primal integral than existing start primal heuristics.

problem: Long reasoning chains in LRMs often contain redundancy uncorrelated with correctness; computational efficiency and real-time applications suffer from excessive thinking.
approach: SAGE sampling paradigm reveals that LRMs implicitly know when to stop thinking; integrating SAGE into group-based RL (SAGE-RL) incorporates efficient patterns into standard pass@1 inference.
contribution: Markedly enhances reasoning accuracy and efficiency across multiple challenging mathematical benchmarks by unleashing efficient reasoning potential.

problem: Composed image retrieval using reference images plus natural-language edits requires preserving fine-grained cues while capturing implicit user intent and avoiding repetition.
approach: Pix2Key represents queries and candidates as open-vocabulary visual dictionaries enabling intent-aware matching; V-Dict-AE self-supervised pretraining improves dictionary representation without CIR supervision.
contribution: Improves Recall@10 up to 3.2 points on DeepFashion-MM; additional V-Dict-AE gain of 2.3 points with improved intent consistency and maintained list diversity.
